articleTitle: Optimal allocation of hydrogen-electric hybrid energy storage capacity in microgrid considering capacity degradation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The capacity allocation optimization of the energy storage system is an effective means to realize the absorption of renewable energy and support the safe and stable operation of a high proportion of new energy power systems. This paper constructs a microgrid structure including wind-power generation and hydrogen-electric hybrid energy storage. It proposes an optimization method for capacity allocation of the power grid system, which considers the battery capacity degradation. The method aims to improve the power economy, promote the consumption of new energy generation, and guarantee the stability and security of the power grid. It constructs the power grid capacity allocation optimization model with the power grid investment and operation cost, the battery capacity degradation, power supply stability, and green energy utilization as the objective functions. Experiments verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Time-adaptive Transient Stability Prediction Method Using Convolutional Neural Network and Confidence Interval
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel time-adaptive prediction method based on convolutional neural network (CNN) and confidence interval in order to improve the reliability of transient stability prediction (TSP). With acquiring the generator rotor angle from PMUs, the CNN model is first designed for both quantitative and qualitative TSP. In this way, by estimating the confidence interval of predicted value for CNN model, it determines the critical stability interval in quantitative analysis. Finally, the time-adaptive TSP aimed at those cases at the critical steady state can be implemented by continuous prediction. The case studies have been carried on an IEEE 50-machine and 145-bus system with the help of Matlab® software. The results from the proposed method indicate it improves the reliability of prediction results.

articleTitle: Vulnerability Assessment of Important Infrastructure of Power Grid to Natural Disasters Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: As a typical complex network, the consequence of the accident is not simple equipment damage or regional power failure. Due to its cascading fault characteristics, some damages in the network may cause damage to equipment in other adjacent areas and lead to a wider range of power outages. Based on the theory of multi-attribute evaluation, complex network theory, and disaster science, this research qualitatively analyzes the composition and influencing factors of power grid vulnerability. It quantifies the multi-attribute composition of natural disaster vulnerability and then puts forward the corresponding evaluation methods and models. On this basis, the vulnerability of the power grid is comprehensively evaluated. The experimental results show that the natural disaster vulnerability assessment model of the important infrastructure of the power grid constructed in this paper considers the risk, reliability, and importance of the power grid. The identification accuracy of up to 80% shows that the evaluation path of power grid reconfiguration optimization and power grid optimal configuration given by the model can maximize the overall optimization of power grid operation.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Authentication Scheme in Electric Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The traditional authentication mechanism incurred higher computation and communication overhead, which is not applicable for terminal devices directly in Electric Internet of Things because of limited computing and storage resources. We propose a lightweight mutual authentication scheme for the terminal devices in Electric Internet of Things. The scheme combines both symmetric with asymmetric cryptography algorithms, only through two handshakes, which can achieve mutual authentication between the terminal devices, and effectively resist the attacker's replaying, tampering and injection attacking. The analysis demonstrates that the computational and communication overhead is less than those of similar mechanisms, which is opportune for resource-limited terminal in Electric Internet of Things.

articleTitle: Research on the Transmission Relationship of Grid Science and Technology Innovation Indicators under the Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In recent years, the power industry is committed to clean and low-carbon transformation and development, continues to increase investment in research and development, and innovation capacity has been significantly enhanced, which has strongly supported national energy security and protection. The digital and intelligent upgrading of the industry has become an inevitable trend for the future development of the electric power industry. This paper starts from the grid science and technology innovation index system under the smart grid, based on the improved TrustRank-ISM model to study the conduction relationship and correlation between science and technology innovation indexes, and better explores the relationship between science and technology innovation and smart grid construction from specific indexes, which is conducive to the grid to further improve the science and technology innovation index system and increase the application of key core technologies, to promote the smart grid construction and This will contribute to the low-carbon and green development of energy.

articleTitle: Research on application of high reliability structure in medium voltage distribution network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In recent years, some provincial companies are actively exploring and optimizing the medium voltage grid structure around the improvement of high reliability and flexibility of the 10 kV distribution network. These provincial companies have come up with a variety of unique mid-and low-voltage distribution network structures, such as the double petal of Beijing's urban sub-centre, the snow net of Tianjin, the double petal and four-corner-six connection of Xiongan, Hebei, the diamond-type of Shanghai, the honeycomb of Weihai, Shandong and the star-type of Zhengzhou, Henan, and carry out pilot construction application. These practices for the determination of provincial companies 10 kV target grid provides a reference. At present, the above-mentioned grid structure of the double petal, snow net, diamond-type three types of structures have been built in Beijing, Hebei, Tianjin, Shanghai pilot areas put into operation. Based on the analysis of the above three kinds of grid structures, such as their development patterns and characteristics, their construction conditions and actual operation efficiency, the paper puts forward some suggestions on the application of grid structures.

articleTitle: Research on Partition Method of Distributed Photovoltaic Cluster Based on Modularity Index and Absorption Ability
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: To achieve large-scale renewable energy, grid friendly coordination and the need to maximize grid-connection and consumption functions, the clustering method has become a forward-looking solution for distribution network planning, construction and dispatching control. In this paper, the modularity index and active power balance index based on electrical distance are taken as the comprehensive classification index. Then genetic algorithm is introduced to divide the distributed PV cluster in the distribution network. Finally, a 10kV distribution system is taken as an example, and the distributed photovoltaic cluster planning is simulated and analyzed, which proves that the distributed photovoltaic cluster division method is effective.

articleTitle: Decentralized Demand Management of Industrial Parks with Dynamic Load Resources Commitment
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The prevalence of renewable generators poses great challenges to the dynamic balancing of the power grid. As a promising solution to locally accommodate renewable energy generation, the operation of flexible resources has become an important problem. In this paper, we focus on utilizing demand-side resources in an industrial park to consume the renewable energy generation locally, with a decentralized algorithm. One critical issue in the decentralized demand management is the uncertain willingness of demand-side resources to participate, which is usually ignored in the existing literature. To fill the research gap, we propose a convex optimization model for the demand management problem in industrial parks, and design a consensus-based demand management algorithm to handle the addition and deletion of load resources during the demand management process. In the case study, we simulate the decentralized demand management in an industrial park, and compare the results obtained by the proposed algorithm with the benchmarks. Our proposed method can effectively handle the dynamic commitment of load resources in the industrial park and converges to the global optimal solutions in different scenarios.

articleTitle: Electrical Final Design for a Large Hydropower Station in Africa
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The Hydropower Project is located on the Rufiji River in the southeast of the United Republic of Tanzania, Africa, with a total installed capacity of 2,115MW. Taking into account the hydrological and meteorological characteristics, kinetic energy characteristics, construction scale, requirements for connecting to the power system, overall layout of the hub, operating conditions, and equipment characteristics of the project, the combination combination connection mode of the generator-main transformer is one unit and one transformer unit connection, and the 400 kV high voltage single line diagram will be double bus-bars with two longitudinal sectionalizers configuration. The design of main electrical connection, service power system, main electrical equipment selection, over-voltage prevention, earthing system and lighting system of the power station are introduced.

articleTitle: Protection Device Platform Design Adapted to Distributed Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The distributed smart grid realizes the upgrading and transformation of the distribution network form by serving the development of new energy. The new power grid form puts forward new requirements for protection devices. In this paper, a protection device adapted to the construction of distributed smart grid is designed, which can accept the current and voltage analog signals collected by substations, convert them into several digital signals after AC/DC conversion, and identify different fault types of distributed smart grids under the background of clean energy access to the power system after processed by relay protection algorithms in the chip. The device is composed of a protection measurement module, input circuit, output loop, chip, communication loop, and human-machine interface loop, and this paper gives the detailed circuit interface design and equipment selection of each module, which is of great significance to the construction of distributed smart grid.

articleTitle: Operation strategy of Virtual power plant based on scale and flexible resource layering and zoning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Under the "dual carbon" strategy, actively managing dispersed, diverse, and massive flexible resources has become one of the important tasks in the construction of new power systems. Virtual power plant provides a new management mode with high flexibility and adaptability. This paper analyzes the operation characteristics of flexible resources in Virtual power plant, stratified them based on the response time, transfer cost and response capacity of flexible resources, and zoned flexible resources based on the regulation requirements of the power system, and formulated a dynamic layered and zoned operation strategy for Virtual power plant, And the effectiveness of the hierarchical partitioning strategy was demonstrated through peak shaving scenarios.

articleTitle: A method for analyzing the response behavior of central air conditioning based on senseless demand response
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The share of air conditioning loads in electricity end-use equipment is growing year on year and has become the most important component of peak loads, deepening the contradiction between supply and demand during peak hours in China and leading to a further widening of the peak-valley differential. However, at the same time, air conditioning loads have a certain thermal storage capacity and have a huge potential for load regulation, which can be incorporated into the dispatch of the power system through demand response in order to improve the willingness and satisfaction of central air conditioning users to participate in demand response, this paper proposes a method to analyze the response behavior of central air conditioning based on senseless demand response. Firstly, a senseless demand response platform is constructed, secondly, the thermodynamic model of the room in which the central air conditioning is located is analyzed, then the response potential of the central air conditioning is analyzed. Finally, a simulation is carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Long Short-Term Memory Network-Based Method for Frequency Security Boundary Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the increasing level of grid-connected renewable energy, the system parameters tend to be highly time-varying. In order to safeguard the system frequency, existing studies use data-driven or system frequency response models to predict the dynamic frequency after it is subjected to disturbances, which can be used to determine whether to take appropriate frequency control measures to prevent frequency collapse based on the prediction results, but it is still a frequency prediction after a disturbance occurs and cannot assess the system’s ability to resist the disturbance before it occurs. Unlike existing studies, we first define the concept of frequency security boundary, which can characterize the ability of system frequency to resist the disturbance before frequency events. After that, a long short-term memory network-based method is proposed for predicting the frequency security boundary, by offline training and online prediction. Finally, a test model is built in MATLAB and the effectiveness of the method in this paper is verified.

articleTitle: Research on microgrid protection algorithm considering transition resistance
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Microgrid is the focus of electrical system reform in the world, and its fault characteristics are different from distribution network, so the traditional protection scheme is no longer suitable for microgrid. Aiming at the influence of transition resistance on the measured impedance in microgrid protection, a new distance protection scheme with a certain degree of resistance to transition resistance is proposed according to the voltage and current changes at the fault occurs before and after the two ends of the line. First, a small resistance is placed between the protection installation points, thereby weakening the influence of the transition resistance on the line. Secondly, according to the phase relationship between fault current and measured current, a new adaptive tuning coefficient is constructed, which can eliminate the influence of transition resistance on measured impedance to some extent. In this paper, based on real-time data simulation of PSCAD/EMTDC platform, a microgrid system is constructed to simulate the size of transition resistance when ground fault occurs. The comparison of simulation data shows that the scheme has certain characteristics of transition resistance, has certain reliability, and increases the range of protection actions.

articleTitle: A Track Filtering Algorithm Based on α − β Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Track filtering is to smooth the current state of the target according to the existing valid observations and predict the next state of the target. Whether the selection of the track filtering algorithm is reasonable has an important influence on whether the correct track can be obtained. In this paper, the main method of α − β filtering gain calculation under multi-target tracking is given. MATLAB simulation is designed for radar detection scenarios such as tracking low and slow small UAVs. Data processing and analysis of simulation results prove that α − β filtering effectively reduces measurement error and improves detection accuracy. Finally, the simulation results are verified by comparing the measured radar data before and after adding the radar track filtering.

articleTitle: Research on power grid equipment disaster loss model based on "strong wind and heavy rain" combined disaster
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper comprehensively considers the evolution characteristics and recurrence laws of urban power grid complex disasters, studies the superimposed amplified damage effects of natural disasters of different causes on power grid equipment in the time domain and the space domain, and builds a multi-physical field dynamic simulation model of complex disasters. Aiming at the coupling mechanism of power grid damage under the simultaneous action of multiple physical fields, such as strong wind and rainstorm load, land seepage, flood and waterlogging, the mechanical modeling is carried out to solve the problem of single factor in power grid disaster loss assessment under complex disaster scenarios, and to lay the theoretical and technical foundation for improving the disaster prevention and mitigation ability of power grid equipment in actual complex environments.

articleTitle: Internal electricity price formulation strategy and energy optimal scheduling of virtual power plant
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the increasing adoption of renewable energy sources like wind power and photovoltaics, traditional energy consumers are becoming energy producers and consumers with their own generation capabilities. However, this transition has raised concerns about the limited availability of flexible resources in the power system. In response, the concept of virtual power plants has emerged as a solution to optimize the utilization of these resources. By aggregating and centrally managing distributed generation and consumption assets, virtual power plants enable local integration of renewable energy, reduce peak loads, and lower energy costs. This paper presents the design of a virtual power plant integrated with new energy generation technologies and proposes a two-layer optimization model. The upper layer focuses on achieving cost-effective interaction between the virtual power plant and the grid, while the lower layer optimizes the energy consumption of generation and consumption devices based on internal purchase prices. The optimization model is solved using a combination of genetic algorithms and Yalmip+Cplex. Results indicate that the proposed approach significantly reduces energy costs for both generation and consumption devices, facilitating increased local integration of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheduling Method for Heterogeneous Loads Considering Load Rebound and Control Cost
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: How to coordinate large-scale adjustable flexible load resources to participate in the operation and control of the power system has become a new challenge faced by the power system. However, there is relatively little research on the optimization scheduling of heterogeneous load groups within aggregators, and the rebound effect and control cost of load groups have not been considered. Therefore, this paper firstly establishes a virtual energy storage model for air-conditioning, electric vehicle, and energy storage. Secondly, a hierarchical optimization scheduling architecture is established: the upper layer optimizes the scheduling of aggregators based on non-cooperative games, while the lower layer allocates the reduction of heterogeneous load groups within the aggregator considering load rebound effect and control cost. Finally, the superiority of the proposed method is verified through an example. The example shows that the proposed optimization scheduling method can effectively control load rebound and reduce control cost.

articleTitle: Definition and Analysis of the Frequency Security Boundary Dominated by Frequency Nadir
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The introduction of renewable energy sources will change the inertia and the ability of power systems to resist disturbances. Systems with different penetration levels of renewable energy may have unstable frequency after suffering different disturbance events, which endanger the frequency security of power systems. To address the above problems, and in order to evaluate the ability of the system frequency to resist disturbances, this paper proposes the concept of frequency security boundary, i.e., the maximum unbalanced power that can be tolerated by the system within the frequency security constraint. Meanwhile, this paper further analyzes the effects of renewable energy with different frequency control types and different control gains on the frequency security boundaries, by taking virtual inertia and droop control as examples. Finally, this paper establishes the frequency response model with different frequency control types in MATLAB. The simulation results show that renewable energy with frequency control can expand the system frequency security boundary.

articleTitle: Airborne LiDAR-based Wind Deflection Check for Power Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Wind deflection faults in transmission lines are an undeniable reality that can disrupt the normal operation of power systems. To address this issue and ensure the continuous and reliable functioning of transmission lines, this paper proposes an innovative approach: an airborne LiDAR-based wind deflection check method. By acknowledging the occurrence of wind deflection faults, we aim to develop a solution that effectively mitigates their impact and enhances the overall stability of power systems. The extraction and single-component segmentation of power lines are achieved by using a linear extraction algorithm based on principal components and an improved region growth segmentation algorithm for the filtered. The Euclidean clustering method is used to segment other components to obtain the point cloud data of each type of component monomer. The point cloud data are used to measure the basic attribute information and location information of the components. The experiments use UAVs with airborne LiDAR to select transmission lines in a certain region for data scanning and processing. The experimental results show that the method in this paper can realize fast and effective wind deflection checking of transmission lines, which can be done in a certain region for data scanning and processing. The experimental results show that the method in this paper can realize fast and effective wind deflection checking of transmission lines, which helps to realize reconstruction, localization, and early warning of transmission lines in 3D scenes.

articleTitle: Dynamic flexible networking and optimal scheduling for AC/DC hybrid distribution network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Dynamic flexible networking and optimal scheduling model for the AC/DC hybrid distribution network is proposed in this paper. In order to achieve optimal matching of source and load resources and minimum network active power loss, the model considers the flexible networking constraints of the AC/DC hybrid distribution network, the dynamic network reconfiguration (DNR) constraints of the AC/DC hybrid distribution network, power flow constraints, and photovoltaic constraints. The dynamic flexible networking and optimal scheduling scheme can be obtained by solving the linearized model through Gurobi solver. Finally, the improved IEEE 33-node system is used for simulation, and the result shows that the proposed scheme can significantly reduce the network active power loss.

Author Keywords: mixed integer second order cone programming

articleTitle: Research on air conditioning load prediction based on LSTM neural network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Accurate prediction of air conditioning load is important for developing demand-side response as air conditioning load is increasingly higher. An LSTM-based prediction model for air conditioning load was constructed and compared to the conventional BP model. The ARIMA model, which was found to have higher prediction accuracy, suggests that the model is more generalized and of great value for application.

articleTitle: Dependence of tunnel magnetoresistance effects of MgO based magnetic tunnel junctions on magnetron sputtering parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: MgO based magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) were fabricated by magnetron sputtering single crystal MgO target. The (001) crystal structure of MgO film can be obtained under less than 6 cm parallel distance between MgO target and substrate. Lots of MgO based MTJs have more than 100% TMR values at the distance of 5 cm and annealing temperature 320360 ℃ from the statistical perspective. However, MTJs show almost zero TMR values at the distance ranging from 6 to 10 cm. MTJs deposited with 30° angle and 6 cm distance between MgO target and the substrate have 24-52% TMR values, indicating that the off-axis deposition helps to improve (001) MgO crystal structure. Although the adjustment of RF power (100-220W) and Ar work pressure (12-15 mTorr) can slightly affect TMR values of MTJs, yet the distance between MgO target and substrate is the more sensitive parameter. Therefore, the depositing distance between MgO target and substrate need be carefully considered in the fabrication of MgO based MTJs.

articleTitle: A Power Peak Load Forecasting Model Based on Data Mining Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The security of power supply has always been a key concern in the field of electricity, and ensuring the balance between power supply and demand is an important basis for social and economic development. Under the requirement of power balance, it is important to realize the time of peak load appearance and the accurate prediction of the load value. In this paper, we start from the distribution of power peaks, find the third quarter with the most peaks and the greatest impact through statistical analysis, and use k-means clustering analysis to divide the load into three parts: climate load affected by temperature and basic and variable load not affected by temperature, and establish a regression prediction model relying on GDP, average temperature and load time series data in the second quarter by combining the principle of gray prediction to achieve The purpose of locating and predicting the annual load peaks is to provide a reference for power resource allocation and dispatch. The model is designed to forecast the time and value of annual load peaks and provide a reference for power resource allocation and dispatch.

articleTitle: Transmission expansion planning considering customer interests for wind power integration in electricity power market
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The high penetration of variable renewable energy sources (RES) in the power system poses substantial risks to the operation of the electricity power market. How to ensure the stability and economy of power market operation while consuming RES is a great challenge for transmission expansion planning (TEP). In this paper, we propose a price signal-based planning model that takes into account the interests of the customer side, which can promote the consumption of RES, effectively cope with the price fluctuations caused by the volatility of RES, suppress the price spikes and reduce the price risks of the customer side.

articleTitle: Current inversion method for TMR array based on particle swarm optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: According to the current measurement requirements of rectangular copper bars in smart grids, a current inversion scheme based on particle swarm optimization algorithm is proposed for array current sensors. Calculate the spatial magnetic field generated by the copper bar current through simulation. The magnetic field is obtained with a measurement array based on TMR sensors, and the rectangular copper bar current is calculated by using a particle swarm optimization algorithm based on the measured values of tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) sensors. Simulation results show that this scheme improves the accuracy of current inversion compared to traditional average algorithm.

articleTitle: Micro Electric Field Sensor Based on Piezoelectric and Piezoresistive Coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Electric field information is a fundamental physical quantity in power systems, and electric field measurement is indispensable for the structural design and insulation testing of electrical equipment, so electric field measurement is a very important task. In this paper, we propose a miniature electric field sensor structure based on the piezoelectric-piezoresistive effect and the interface coupling mechanism between them. The piezoelectric effect converts the electric field into a deformation of the piezoelectric crystal, which drives the vibration of the semiconductor piezoresistive film through the interface coupling between the materials, thus causing the resistance of the doped region of the piezoresistive film to change, and the external electric field can be inferred by measuring the change in resistance using a Wheatstone bridge. To verify the feasibility of this electric field sensor, a simulation was performed by using COMSOL Multiphysics, and we also designed the manufacturing process of the device. The simulation results show that the electric field sensor has a good electric field response and is expected to be applied to electric field measurement on a large scale in the future.

articleTitle: Research on Low Voltage Ride Through Control Strategy of Wind Power Grid-connected Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In order to improve the operating stability and low voltage ride through (LVRT) ability of wind power system, this paper studies the control strategy of voltage source grid-connected inverter of doubly-fed wind power system. First of all, the main functions of grid-connected inverter in wind power system are analyzed, and the research status and unsolved problems of wind power grid-connected inverter control technology at home and abroad are discussed. Secondly, this paper introduces the basic principle of the first-order linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) technology. Then, On the basis of the double closed-loop proportion integration (PI) controller model, the voltage outer loop is improved based on the first order active disturbance rejection strategy. Finally, the steady-state and symmetrical voltage drop conditions are studied through the simulation model, and the voltage and current waveforms of the power grid are analyzed to verify the practicability and low voltage crossing ability of the first-order linear active disturbance rejection control technology.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Evaluation for AC/DC Distribution Networks with High Proportion of Distributed Energy Resources Access
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: A high proportion of distributed energy resources (DERs) access to distribution networks brings more challenges to the operation of distribution networks while promoting the cleanliness of the power system. AC/DC hybrid distribution network (HDN) is attracting more attention because of the flexible power transfer capability and significant advantages in the consumption of distributed energy sources. However, HDNs differ in terms of topology, operation, and regulation compared to AC networks. Therefore, the comprehensive evaluation of HDNs is an urgent issue to be addressed. An evaluation method for HDNs considering the access of large-scale DERs is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the typical structures of HDNs are summarized. Secondly, the evaluation system of HDNs is established, taking into account the problems caused by distributed energy resources to the distribution network. Finally, the evaluation of HDNs is achieved by means of the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). The case study selects an actual HDN as the simulation background and conducts a comprehensive evaluation of the AC/DC interconnection system.

articleTitle: Quantitative and apportionment method of auxiliary service cost of new energy subject
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The large-scale access of new energy power has caused a rapid increase in the demand for auxiliary services. The original auxiliary service cost sharing mechanism cannot meet the market requirements, and the supply of auxiliary services is reduced, resulting in a decline in the security and stability of the power grid. It is urgent to consider the new mechanism of auxiliary service cost sharing. In this paper, considering the factors of new energy access, the calculation formula of auxiliary service capacity and cost caused by new energy access is established. By considering the marginal contribution of inter-subject to the increase of cost, the cost allocation model based on Shapley value method is established, and the allocation model between new energy power generation subject and load is deduced. The allocation model reflects the responsibility of each subject, which conforms to the principle of ' who benefits, who shares ', and helps to improve the enthusiasm of service providers to provide corresponding auxiliary services, thereby increasing the stability of power grid operation.

articleTitle: Calculation Method of Power and Electricity Balance Considering Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Demand response is an important means to tap the flexibility of the user side. Through demand response, the power load can "move with the wind and light", thus reducing the volatility of the net load curve. Therefore, the participation of demand response in power and energy balance is a new idea to solve the problem of power and energy balance, whose main role is to ensure supply and promote consumption. In this paper, through the method of time series production simulation, two methods of pre demand response and post demand response are constructed to calculate a provincial grid by five years from 2025 to 2060. The calculation results show that post demand response can effectively improve the power shortage of the system, significantly promote the consumption of new energy sources and reduce carbon emissions of the system. The pre demand response will not necessarily improve the power shortage of the system, and has little effect on promoting new energy consumption and reducing carbon emissions of the system.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation Method of Novel Distribution Network Based on Combination Weighting Method
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: It is of great practical significance to establish a distribution network evaluation method suitable for China’s national conditions and evaluate it scientifically and reasonably in order to realize the sustainable development of China’s power system. This paper comprehensively evaluates it from three aspects: reliability, power quality and economy, and puts forward an evaluation method of low carbon and equipment status based on 5 aspects and 18 indexes. On this basis, a new evaluation index system-entropy weight index system-fuzzy comprehensive evaluation system is put forward. Taking the distribution network of three regions in Liaoning as an example, it shows that the novel distribution network planning scheme proposed in this paper can not only explain the current novel distribution network planning scheme but also lay the foundation for the formulation and implementation of the planning scheme in the future.

articleTitle: Analysis of a 110kV Transformer Near-Area Short-Circuit Fault Resulting in Winding Deformation and Management Measures
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper provides some suggestions for the safe, reliable and economic operation of the transformer by studying and analysing a case in which a 110kV transformer was destabilized due to a short-circuit fault in the proximity of the medium voltage side of the transformer, which resulted in the main transformer destabilisation. Firstly, the real cause of the transformer failure is analysed by detailed analysis of the transformer failure process, test and disassembly verification. In addition, by collecting the detailed structural parameter table of the faulty transformer, and further using the self-developed VIT calibration platform system modelling simulation calculation, the actual ability of the transformer to withstand the short-circuit current is not as good as the theoretical withstand value provided by the manufacturer. Finally, for the operating transformers, passive management measures are proposed in terms of irregular short-circuit resistance calibration, segmented operation of medium and low-voltage busbars, neutral point addition of small reactance grounding, addition of current-limiting reactors, and return to the factory (on-site) for overhaul; for the non-networked transformers, proactive management recommendations are proposed in terms of quality control in advance of the network entry, design of the transformer, raw material selection, and requirements of the manufacturing process.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis and Current Estimation of Current Sensors for Asynchronous Motors Based on Student’s T Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The asynchronous motor system performance will deteriorate significantly when the current sensor is faulty. And because the asynchronous motor has the characteristics of nonlinearity and high coupling in practical application, the system noise is generally non-Gaussian noise. So, it is of good meaning to discuss the current sensor fault diagnosis and correction problem of the asynchronous motor in the case of non-Gaussian noise. Firstly, coordinate transformation is used to determine whether the current sensor is breakdown. When both two-phase current sensors are faulty, a new kind of current estimation method is designed, for the asynchronous motor system with the noise satisfying the Student’s t distribution. A non-Gaussian current sensor correction method is given to obtain the state estimate of phase current and replace the measurement of the current sensor affected by the fault. The given method is compared with the pre-existing Luenberger observer. Simulation results indicate that the designed method has the advantage over the Luenberger observer.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Self-healing Simulation of Shipboard Zonal Distribution Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper uses MATLAB/Simulink to build a fault self-healing simulation model of shipboard zonal distribution power system, uses LabVIEW's MIT toolkit and MATLAB script controls to seamlessly connect LabVIEW with MATLAB/Simulink, and completing the communication between multiple industrial computers based on TCP/IP protocol. Designing a reconfiguration strategy based on an improved particle swarm algorithm to achieve self-healing of short-circuit faults in distribution networks and a compensation strategy based on a sliding mode observer to achieve propulsion motor speed sensor fault compensation. Completing a fault self-healing simulation system for the shipboard zonal distribution power system. The actual simulation experiment shows that the self-healing simulation system has the characteristics of high timeliness and stable operation.

articleTitle: A Control Strategy for Enhancing the Transient Stability of SOP System Based on Virtual Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Soft open points (SOPs) offer real-time power flows control, the rapid self-healing of faults, and the balance of feeder load, which are widely applied in the distribution networks (DNs). However, distribution networks based on SOP often suffer from large signal disturbances such as grid voltage dips (GVDs) during operation, and their stability needs to be further improved to ensure the safe and stable operation of the SOP system. This article proposes a stable control strategy based on virtual capacitors and verifies the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis using mixed potential theory (MPT). Firstly, the virtual capacitor control strategy proposed in this article that can enhance the stability of SOP systems is stated. Secondly, a nonlinear average model of SOP was established, and based on MPT, the large signal stability criteria (LSSC) for the SOP system using virtual capacitor control strategy were derived. Based on this criterion, the impact of DC side capacitance on system stability was analyzed, and the effectiveness of virtual capacitance strategy to enhance the system's stable operation capability was verified. Finally, the correctness of the obtained criteria and the feasibility and effectiveness of the virtual capacitor strategy were verified through Matlab/Simulink time-domain simulation.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Optimal Operation Strategy of Virtual Power Plant Considering Renewable Energy Consumption Rate
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: As the scale of virtual power plant (VPP) continues to expand, the problem of VPP operating expenditure costs and distributed renewable energy accommodation rate can not be optimized at the same time becomes more and more prominent. To address this problem, this paper establishes a multi-objective optimization operation model for VPP, taking into account the constraints of renewable energy output, storage battery output, etc., and aiming at minimizing the daily operating cost and maximizing the accommodation rate of renewable energy. Then, the model is solved by the multi-objective optimization algorithm and compared and analyzed with the optimization results under a single objective to verify the effectiveness of the proposed multi-objective optimization operation strategy.

articleTitle: Distributed Differential Protection for Distribution Automation Based on 5G Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In this paper, firstly, the business characteristics of the distribution network are sorted out, and the demand of power business for 5G communication is analyzed. Thus, a 5G distribution scheme is established. On this basis, a distributed distribution differential protection scheme based on 5G edge calculation is proposed for the monitoring ability of distributed power supply and differential protection of the distribution network. In this scheme, the multi-access edge computing server and distributed power supply monitoring are used. The monitoring information unloading model of differential protection with joint communication and calculation is designed. The delay optimization problem of differential protection under the constraints of computing power and power is established, and a solution is proposed by combining the alternating optimization algorithm. The time delay of differential protection tasks under different conditions is simulated and analyzed. The results show that the scheme can effectively reduce the time delay of differential protection.

articleTitle: The Impact of Three-phase Unbalance in Power Grid on the Losses of Distribution Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: As power systems undergo continuous advancement, an increasing number of imbalanced loads are being introduced. The presence of three-phase unbalanced currents in distribution equipment, such as power lines and transformers, gives rise to supplementary losses, resulting in economic challenges like power losses and safety concerns. However, there is limited research on losses in the context of three-phase unbalanced power quality environments. Taking into account the influence of three-phase unbalanced currents flowing through conductors, this study investigates the distribution of currents in each phase and explores the impact of different levels of three-phase unbalance on typical distribution equipment. A calculation method for equivalent losses of conductors considering three-phase unbalance is proposed. Moreover, the energy usage of conventional equipment in the distribution grid is taken into account. Utilizing a theoretical calculation model, a simulation platform is constructed to perform experimental measurements on equipment losses under diverse imbalanced currents. This enables the reciprocal validation of the theoretical calculation model and experimental data. The study investigates the typical attributes of three-phase imbalance and its influence on losses in the distribution grid.

articleTitle: Analytical Current Injection Feasible Region and Transient Stability Enhancement Control for PLL Synchronized VSC During Low Voltage Grid Fault
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: How to analysis the phase-locked loop synchronous (PLL-Syn) transient stability issue in weak grid connected VSC system (WG-VSCs), and further guide the transient stability enhancement control design is of significance to the WG-VSCs, which is also the main motivation of this paper. First, from the perspective of ensuring PLL-Syn transient stability, the concept of the current injection feasible region (CIFR) is proposed for the first time. Moreover, a modified equal area criterion is utilized to obtain the analytical boundary of the feasible region, which can be significantly affected by the indefinite damping of PLL. To expand the CIFR and improve the PLL-Syn transient stability, a simple enhancement control is proposed. Eventually, the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation is performed to validate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Battery Energy Storage Station Group Schedulin Strategy Considering Battery Life Loss
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The large-scale group application of battery energy storage station (BESS) is pivotal in supporting the implementation of carbon neutrality policy. BESS group can promote the grid connection and local consumption of renewable energy. However, excessive battery life loss will compromise the safety and economics of BESS group. In order to ensure the safe and efficient operation, a BESS group scheduling strategy considering battery life loss is proposed in this work. Firstly, the battery life loss is quantified based on the state-of-health (SOH) degradation curve. Then, an BESS group optimization scheduling model is constructed as quadratic programming (QP) problem, considering both state-of-charge (SOC) equalization and battery life loss. Finally, the BESS group scheduling strategy is demonstrated by the numerical simulation of a real-world BESS group. The simulation results prove that the proposed strategy can increase the safety and operational efficiency of BESS group.

articleTitle: Simulation on Multiple Wind Farm Power Series Based on Spatiotemporal Markov Process
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With increasing proportion of wind power integrated in the power system, operation simulation analysis has become an important tool for power system planning and operation. This paper presents a statistical modeling scheme for the stochastic time series of multiple wind farms power considering both the temporal patterns and the spatial correlation. The proposed composite spatiotemporal Markov process model is composed of a temporal Markov process with inter-day modal transfer, and multiple spatial Markov processes to reflect the correlation among wind farms. Evaluation on the simulation results through statistical metrics showed the feasibility and performance of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Cross-Region Federated Architecture Distributed Service Tracing for Business Middle Platform of New Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper introduce the importance and role of the business middle platform in supporting the digitalization of new power systems. The business middle platform system based on microservices faces some challenges in problem localization and service performance monitoring. The two-tier deployment structure also determines that traditional tracing systems cannot meet the requirements for end-to-end monitoring. To address these challenges, a new design for a distributed service tracing monitoring system with a cross-region federated architecture is proposed. The new solution can both distribute the storage pressure of monitoring data across different regions and perform comprehensive analysis on cross-region service calls. The key to implementing this solution is to expand the traditional span data attributes and federated coordination query capabilities.

articleTitle: Ordered power consumption decision model considering multiple time scales
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In the face of the shortage of power supply from time to time, orderly power consumption is still the normal management work to ensure a stable power supply order in China. At present, most of the orderly power consumption management is based on experience, ignoring the load characteristics of each user, lacking a scientific and effective theoretical basis, causing a lot of inconvenience to the normal life and work of users, and affecting user satisfaction. Based on the load form of the power system and its peak-valley fluctuation characteristics, this paper constructs an orderly power consumption decision-making model through the flexible call of load management means at multiple time scales. The aim is to maximize the load rate and reduce the gap between power supply and demand and achieve a win-win situation of economic and social benefits.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimization of microgrid based on improved ant lion optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: A microgrid energy optimization management method with an improved ant-lion optimization algorithm is proposed for the multi-objective optimal microgrid configuration, making the microgrid operation more efficient, economical, and reasonable. A two-tier energy optimization management is established, with the optimization objectives of micro point network operation cost-benefit, active power loss, and carbon emission. The upper layer uses a fuzzy management system to determine the microgrid operation mode, and the lower layer uses an improved ant-lion optimization algorithm to optimize energy management. Adaptive weights are then invoked to improve the antlion diversity and convergence accuracy. The rationality and effectiveness of the energy management method, the optimization model, and the improved antlion algorithm in this paper are verified by comparing the gray wolf and whale algorithms.

articleTitle: Intelligent Clustering Based Active Power Allocation Strategy for Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of uneven distribution of active power of each unit in a wind farm, an artificial intelligence clustering method based active power distribution strategy of wind turbine is proposed. Firstly, according to the actual operation data of the wind farm, the Pearson correlation coefficient is used to select the clustering data. Then, the Gaussian mixture model is used for clustering experiments. Finally, according to the clustering results, the distribution method of weight proportional coefficient is adopted to evenly distribute power to all units. The simulation results show that the proposed clustering method has a good evaluation score, and the power allocation strategy based on this can fully meet the scheduling criterias. All units can realize the smooth and orderly power rise and fall in the safe operation state, and avoid the problem of frequent start-stop and overload operation of some units caused by uneven power distribution.

articleTitle: Research on frequency control strategy of combined wind- energy storage system
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Under the high penetration rate of wind power, the power system puts forward technical requirements for the frequency regulation capability of wind farms. Considering that the frequency response capability of the double-fed induction generator (DFIG) is insufficient, it is proposed to combine energy storage (ES) with wind power for system frequency regulation. Based on the frequency characteristic models of the wind farm and the ES system, this paper establishes a prediction model for the over speed control of the wind farm and a prediction model for the electrochemical energy storage system, and optimizes the active power output of the wind turbine and the energy storage system. The strategy is based on the optimal control of the wind turbine output power and ES power variation, and on this basis, an optimal control model considering the ES state of charge (SOC) and power is designed. The simulation results show that the proposed control strategy can not only effectively suppress grid frequency deviation can also coordinate the ES state of charge and frequency control.

articleTitle: Strain Response Research of MEMS Electric Field Sensors with PVDF-based Multilayer Piezoelectric Crystal Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The measurement of electric fields in scenarios such as power consuming devices and transmission lines is a critical task. In this paper, piezoelectric-piezoresistive coupling effect MEMS electric field sensors are constructed using COMSOL. The electric field sensors have a small size, an inverted trapezoidal cavity and a multi-layer material formed by adding PVDF to the top and bottom layers of a single piezoelectric crystal. The strain response of three groups of piezoelectric electric field sensors with single structure and multi-layer structure are calculated and analysed by finite element analysis method, and the improvement of sensor response by multi-layer structure based on PVDF layer is concluded. This research provides important guidance for the design of future MEMS electric field sensors and the selection of piezoelectric crystal materials and structures.

articleTitle: The Design and Application of Intelligent Detection and Management System for Low Voltage Distributed Photovoltaic Metering Box
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In response to the low level of digitalization, informatization, and automation in the detection of low voltage distributed photovoltaic metering box, there are problems such as insufficient analysis of detection data, manual recording of data, difficulty in data traceability, and low level of data application. The article analyzes the traditional detection process and methods of the low voltage distributed photovoltaic metering box. It combines traditional detection methods with IDS intelligent detection system and modularizes the detection process. It then develops an intelligent detection management system for the low voltage distributed photovoltaic metering box, which meets the digitization and automation of detection. Through on-site operation and research, it has been shown that the detection efficiency of this system has been improved by 72% compared to traditional detection methods, effectively reducing the labor intensity of detection personnel. It can also improve the fairness and impartiality of detection results, ensure the consistency of supply, and further improve the detection management level of the low voltage distributed photovoltaic metering box.

articleTitle: Adaptive moment of inertia VSG control strategy tidal power storage microgrid system
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the popularity of inverter-based renewable energy, the stability of low inertia and natural intermittent power generation microgrid has become an important issue, and this paper adopts a hybrid energy storage system of supercapacitors and batteries. The proposed microgrid consists of photovoltaic, tidal power unit, supercapacitor, storage battery and load. The system uses virtual synchronous generator (VSG) technology to simulate the performance of traditional synchronous generator (SG). Because of the fixed moment of inertia and damping coefficient of traditional synchronous generator, the dynamic adjustment ability of grid-connected system is not good. By discussing the mathematical model of the converter, an adaptive inertia control strategy is proposed. This strategy can adjust the inertia in real time when VSG angular velocity deviation is large, optimize the moment of inertia of VSG, and reduce the overshoot of the system. Finally, the whole system is modeled and simulated by MATLABTM platform. The simulation results show that the dynamic response of the adaptive VSG control strategy is good, which demonstrates the effectiveness and superiority of the improved strategy.

articleTitle: Study on the influence of limiting link on the stability of three-phase VSR large disturbance
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The stability analysis of three-phase voltage rectifiers (VSR) is usually carried out by the small-signal method, and the limiting link in the control system is ignored. However, under the large disturbance condition, due to its inherent nonlinear characteristics, the limiting link will be triggered, and its influence on stability cannot be ignored. Therefore, this paper analyzes the influence of VSR's limiting link on the stability under large disturbance conditions, and proposes a design method for the value of the limiting link. Firstly, the VSR system with small signal stability and its control structure are introduced. Then, the influence of nonlinear saturation characteristics of SPWM modulation and limiting elements on the stability of the system under large disturbances was analyzed through time-domain simulation. Finally, based on this, a transient control strategy based on open-loop closed-loop switching control is proposed, and the selection criteria for the limit amplitude in the control system are provided

articleTitle: Design of power grid cloud security terminal protection system based on level protection
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper proposes a new power grid cloud security terminal protection system based on hierarchical protection to enhance power grid cloud security terminal operation. The system design includes the overall structure of the terminal protection system using the Net Framework, a protection module based on level protection, and an access control module for power grid cloud security terminal hardware to improve system protection performance. Additionally, the software component involves constructing a security index system for power grid cloud security terminal protection and evaluating terminal protection security through an ant colony algorithm optimization neural network to determine the security level. Experimental results show that the proposed system accurately identifies security risks with low response delay compared to traditional systems.

articleTitle: Reduced-order Model of Frequency Response Including PLL-based DFIG Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In the existing power system frequency response models, most of them ignore the dynamic process of inertial response of renewable energy generation equipment, which makes the new characteristics of power system frequency dynamics not described. In this paper, we take a doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) as an example and establish its electromechanical time-scale motion equation in the frequency domain from its basic control structure, and extract the active power-frequency branch as the equivalent inertia of the DFIG, and the average frequency response model of the system was developed on this basis. Considering the inconvenience of higher order systems in the analysis, the least squares method is used to reduce the order of the frequency response model. Finally, the above model is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink and the simulation results are analyzed.

articleTitle: Novel Phase-locked loop Method for three-phase power grid based on double complex coefficient filter via cross decoupling
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The significance of the phase-locked loop lies in its role as a crucial method for controlling inverters to achieve grid-connected synchronization. However, the existing quasi-type PLL faces a notable issue: it exhibits inadequate resistance against interference, particularly during shifts in grid voltage frequency. This inadequacy leads to significant errors in both detection frequency and phase. To address this, our paper introduces a novel phase-locked loop. This innovative approach is built upon cross-decoupling double complex coefficient filters. We establish a comprehensive understanding by presenting its small-signal model. Moreover, we delve into the impact of filter parameters on dynamic response and provide insights into the digital implementation strategy. Importantly, our proposed phase-locking algorithm demonstrates consistent performance even under the most challenging power grid conditions. The efficacy of our approach is validated through simulations and experimental results.

articleTitle: Grid gallop analysis using the Euler angle estimation method
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper presents a grid line galloping monitoring system that utilizes an IMU to perceive the occurrence of spinning in overhead trans-mission lines. To continually tracking the natural features of electric delivery lines and towers, this system consists of a 6-axis motion sensor, a microcontroller unit, and a communication unit. To identify and forecast the likelihood of galloping, the IMU data is processed in real-time, and the processed data is sent to a central platform through a 4G network. Data cleaning, linear data correction, and attitude estimate using the Euler angle approach are only a few of the formulas used to determine the frequency as well as the amplitude of power line spinning. A PI controller is used to increase the system’s stability and precision as well as to give experimentation to check the algorithms. The suggested system provides real-time data that enables data-driven judgments and ensures the firmness, dependability, and safety of the electric grid and its constituent parts.

articleTitle: Intelligent Planning Method for Solving Overloaded Feeder of Medium Voltage Distribution Network Based on Pipeline-Gird Coupling and Data Fusion : Intelligent Planning of Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Lack of joint modeling of pipeline and gird may cause the distribution network planning results impractical. To address the issues, an intelligent planning method for overloaded feeder of medium voltage distribution networks is proposed in this paper. Firstly, an undirected graph is utilized to model the pipeline, with geographical information mapped into the model. Besides, a directed graph is utilized to model the power grid, with load mapped into the model. Subsequently, based on the distribution network planning guidelines, an intelligent algorithm is developed, integrating Dijkstra’s algorithm and Grey Wolf Optimization algorithm (GWO). Finally, based on the proposed intelligent planning method, three feasible planning solutions for practical engineering applications are generated automatically, demonstrating adaptability to various scenarios.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Transient Simulation Research on UHVDC Based on Synchronous Condenser
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper builds an electromagnetic transient model of the UHVDC including synchronous condenser system in PSCAD. Due to its excellent dynamic reactive power compensation capability, Synchronous condenser technology has been widely applied in the East China Power Grid. The model is helpful for further study of the system voltage regulation and dynamic stabilization effects. The operation results show that the model reflects truly the actual situation and provide platform for further research on commutation failure and suppression measures.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis of Soft Open Points in Distribution Networks Under Grid Voltage Dips Based on Domain of Attraction Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Soft open point (SOP), as a new type of flexible distribution device that replaces traditional tie switches, can achieve flexible and fast adjustment of network power flow. In order to avoid the instability of the SOP system caused by large disturbances, it is of great significance to analyze the transient stability of the SOP system based on the estimation of the region of attraction (ROA). This article uses Brayton Moser's mixed potential theory to estimate the ROA of the SOP system, and based on this, analyzes the transient stability of the SOP system Firstly, a mixed potential function is established and the ROA of the system is estimated based on it. Secondly, based on ROA, the impact of system parameters on stability and the range boundaries of the system under power disturbances are analyzed. Finally, the correctness of the stability analysis conclusion is verified through Matlab/Simulink time-domain simulation.

articleTitle: Research on ACLs Calculation Method Based on Analysis of User Full Load Data
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In order to implement the national policy requirements for power energy supply guarantee, realize precise load control and normalized demand-side management under orderly electricity consumption, support the construction of new power system, and improve the real-time monitoring capability of load resources in different industries, categories, and types of key measures in the new power load management system, this paper proposes a fast air conditioning load (ACLs) calculation method based on user full load data. This method selects key industries of adjustable air conditioning based on fast air conditioning load calculation, and completes accurate air conditioning load calculation based on precise benchmark load data of industry users. Through comparative analysis of the results, the proposed method can achieve more accurate calculation of air conditioning load.

articleTitle: Calculation model of arc discharge pressure in transformer oil
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Internal short circuit faults in transformers can lead to high-energy arc discharges, resulting in incidents of oil tank rupture, explosion, and fire. The source of transformer explosion accidents is the high-voltage bubbles generated by the gasification and decomposition of transformer oil during high-energy arc discharge. Therefore, studying the mechanism of bubble generation due to arc discharge faults in transformer oil is crucial for understanding the subsequent pressure increase and deformation of the oil tank. In this paper, the evaporation-condensation model is modified to include the chemical reactions of high-temperature decomposed insulating oil. A calculation method based on the modified evaporation-condensation model is proposed to simulate the generation of bubbles in the fluid domain. A three-dimensional simulation model of the oil tank is established to analyze the variation process of bubbles and the pressure changes in the fluid domain after bubble generation. This research provides a reference for studying the mechanism of fault bubble generation in transformer oil and offers a new modeling and calculation method for simulating the change of pressure field during the electric arc discharge process in oil.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Copper Bar Current Solution Based on Magnetic Sensor Array
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In order to study the application of rectangular magnetic sensing arrays in power systems, this paper uses a rectangular copper bar and a wire model to simulate the spatial magnetic field. On this basis, a rectangular magnetic sensor array is used to simulate, measure, and calculate the current of the copper bar. The impact of errors such as crosstalk and sensitivity deviation of the magnetic sensors on the current solution of rectangular copper bars was analyzed. In simulation analysis, the rectangular magnetic sensing array can measure the current of the rectangular copper bar with a theoretical accuracy of ±1%.

articleTitle: Automatic Generation Control of Virtual Power Plant for High-proportion Heterogeneous Distributed Photovoltaics
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In the current virtual power plant (VPP) design schemes, photovoltaic (PV) generator is seen as an indispensable choice. Due to the significant differences in the unit capacity and operating characteristics of PV, the coordination of start-stop PV units and continuously adjustable PV units poses a noteworthy challenge in VPP with high-level PV penetration. To solve the problem, this paper presents an automatic generation control (AGC) instruction allocation algorithm using mixed integer liner programming (MILP) with a special inverter controller of PV. Based on the simulation cases, this algorithm can facilitate effective coordination between start-stop PV units and continuously adjustable PV units within VPP.

articleTitle: Faults of High-voltage Equipment in Substations Based on Temperature Probability Density Thermal Infrared Image Recognition Method
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Aiming at the identification of thermal infrared images of high-voltage equipment failures in substations, a thermal infrared image recognition method is proposed in this paper, which is based on the characteristics of temperature probability density. Firstly, by employing the Kernel function estimation, the heat odds density function of the infrared image is extracted. Secondly, the preliminary classification of detection targets takes into account the physical characteristics of temperature distribution and background composition in the thermal infrared image. Finally, the fault part in the thermal infrared image is extracted by using the K-means clustering method based on a priori knowledge of temperature density probability. The results indicate that the proposed method is capable of enhancing the accuracy of fault location identification in comparison to the traditional clustering method, while also significantly reducing the clustering iterations by more than 50%. This method can provide a theoretical basis for the construction of the substation’s intelligent detection system to ensure the operation reliability of power equipment.

articleTitle: Research on Green and Low Carbon Smart Substation Construction Standard System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: To build a sustainable power network infrastructure and regulate the construction of green and low-carbon smart substations, the establishment of a construction standard system is one of the key tasks in the current power grid construction. This study analyzes the needs of the standard system for green and low-carbon smart substation construction by systematically sorting out the domestic and international technical standards for smart substations and the current situation of green substation standard construction; it designs a new hierarchical structure of the standard system and constructs a general framework of the standard system for green and low-carbon smart substations. For the first time, the study combines green, low-carbon, intelligent and digital concepts into standards, points out the urgent need to develop standards for the construction of the current standard system, and puts forward a focused action plan for standardization work.

articleTitle: A study on Short-Term Electricity Load Forecasting for Industrial Parks method using QPSO-TCN Based on Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the development of power grid big data and industrial automation, the number of nonlinear factors influencing load fluctuations is increasing, complicating accurate prediction. This paper addresses predicting short-term electricity load in industrial parks using a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) model. In the training phase, Quantum Particle Swarm Optimization (QPSO) tunes hyperparameters to improve accuracy. In quantum space, particles search globally, optimizing predictions. For data preprocessing, artificial features like date and weather that influence fluctuations are incorporated. Additionally, AutoEncoder and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) are used to extract load data features. Finally, feature engineering methods are used to select highly correlated inputs, enhancing model learning and interpretability. Simulation results confirm the proposed method significantly improves prediction accuracy compared to traditional industrial park short-term forecasting methods.

Author Keywords: Short-term Load Forecasting for Industrial Parks

articleTitle: Net Load Forecasting Based on Residual Attention CNN-BiLSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Net load forecasting is a crucial task in power system operation and energy management. Accurate prediction of net load helps power companies optimize their generation plans, enhance energy utilization efficiency, and ensure a balance between power supply and demand. To improve the accuracy and precision of net load forecasting, this study proposes a solution based on the Residual Attention CNN-BiLSTM (RA-CNN-BiLSTM) model. The proposed model combines Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) and incorporates the residual attention mechanism to capture important features and temporal relationships in net load forecasting. Experimental comparisons and evaluations demonstrate that the RA-CNNBiLSTM model achieves lower prediction errors in net load forecasting and outperforms other models significantly.

articleTitle: Practice of Forecasting Power Supply and Demand Development Based on Parametric Energy-Environmental Planning Model@@A Case Study in the Main Urban Area of Nanjing
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The energy-environment model is often used to forecast medium and long-term energy trends under environmental boundary conditions, and has good potential for forecasting power supply and demand development with carbon emission limit value. Nanjing, as one of the core cities in the Yangtze River Delta region of China, is a strong economic city with pillar industries including automobile industry, steel industry and petrochemical materials. In recent years, Nanjing's industrial structure and energy consumption structure are undergoing rapid changes, and the position of electric energy in its terminal energy consumption is gradually increasing.
